pr_body:
This PR adds static `QuicConnection.IsSupported` member which can be used to check if the platform is capable of QUIC. The implementation is routed to `MsQuicApi.IsQuicSupported`.

Fixes #65802.

This comment from the issue has info about how to exclude the auto-generated PNSE: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/65802#issuecomment-1050662121

Should be better now. I also tested it by manually copying the "unsupported" `System.Net.Quic.dll` to local testhost bits and MsQuic tests get correctly disabled, while Mock tests throw (since they don't check `IsEnabled` -> I added that in this PR as well). So I am confident this will work as intended.
Also you can look with ILSpy, ildasm, etc. into the content of S.N.Quic.dll for other platforms to check it does have `IsSupported` returning false instead of throwing.

issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: QUIC should have an IsSupported API
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/ncl See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation There is an `SocketsHttpHandler.IsSupported` property. That avoids using the handler on platforms where everything throws PNSE. System.Net.Quic should have a similar property. An extra complication is QUIC has operating system (Win11+), configuration (TLS 1.3 is enabled), and component requirements (additional Linux deps). I'm not sure whether they should be covered by the same property or a different one. e.g. ```csharp public static bool IsSupported { get; } // I wonder if there is a way to have an API that gives a message about what QUIC requirement is missing public static bool HasRequirements { get; } ``` Related issues: * https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/56005 * https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/55237 ### API Proposal ```C# namespace System.Net.Quic { public class QuicConnection { public static bool IsSupported { get; } } } ``` ### API Usage ```C# if (QuicConnection.QuicConnection) { // listen for QUIC connections } ``` ### Alternative Designs _No response_ ### Risks _No response_
Author: JamesNK
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.Net.Http`
Milestone: -

> I'm not sure whether they should be covered by the same property or a different one.

For what it's worth, in the crypto APIs like `ChaCha20Poly1305`, we have an `IsSupported` that covers both platform support and dependencies.
Example of how to exclude some members from auto-generated PNSE: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/cd4157f9024f1cc5c47c4e894842d3e0543f943f

review_comments: Is there an issue for this? If so, we should link it here.

As far as I understand it, we build the S.N.Quic tests only for Linux and Windowsm so they are never run on any of the platforms where we throw PNSE from everything. Thus, the condition was never needed.
But I do agree it doesn't hurt here, and at least it won't break if/when we expand the target OS list.
